items.title: Before Buying a Tiny Home on Amazon, Make Sure You Know the ABCs of ADUs
items.summary:
In recent years, social media has been flooded with videos of folks who’ve purchased a tiny home or accessory dwelling unit (ADU) on Amazon .

Touting to have dropped anywhere between $8,000 to $50,000, these homeowners shared the process of just buying a house with the click of a button, along with whatever else ended up in their carts.

But the reality is, Amazon actually prohibits the sale of habitable tiny homes and prefabricated dwellings. Its Seller Central policy explicitly banned complete prefab homes, tiny house kits marketed as living spaces, modular and container homes, and other factory-built housing units.

Despite that, you’re likely to still find listings for tiny homes on the platform, which makes it even more imperative that you learn the ABCs of ADUs.

An ADU defined 

To begin with, ADUs are additional small housing structures built on a property that already has a main home or main structure. Tiny homes are usually freestanding, compact units typically under 400 square feet—sometimes on foundations or other times on wheels like an RV.

But in both cases, the structures are economical and effective ways to achieve additional living space.

"As urban populations swell and sustainability becomes a central focus, the ability to build smaller, energy-efficient homes with reduced environmental impact will be key," says Paul Dashevsky , co-CEO of Maxable , a leader in ADU planning, building, and development.

But while tiny homes and ADUs may indeed be poised to make a positive impact toward solving the housing crisis , potential buyers need to know that you…
items.t: Before Buying a Tiny Home on Amazon, Make Sure You Know the ABCs of ADUs

items.title: The Home Audit That Could Save Homeowners Thousands—and Cost You Only $50
items.summary:
With housing costs skyrocketing, every little bit helps—and sometimes, there are options even longtime homeowners are unaware of. 

For example, a homeowner recently turned to Reddit to vent about humidity and outdoor air entering their home. They received quotes for an energy audit ranging from $100 to $200 and asked if this service is actually worth it. 

Someone from Connecticut replied saying they paid only $50 for the same type of audit, thanks to a subsidy from their electric company—and depending on your location, utility provider, and/or income, you could also qualify for a subsidized or even free energy audit. 

While experts agree that a $50 assessment is less common, even paying a few hundred for one may save you thousands of dollars down the road. That's because it can uncover hidden air leaks that may contribute to higher utility bills and damaging moisture issues.

“When you seal air leaks, you may prevent water vapor inside your house from turning into liquid inside your walls. This eliminates the need for costly wood rot and mold issues that may lead to $5,000 or more in repairs and reduces wear and tear on your HVAC unit,” explains Andrew Pho , a home renovation and improvement expert at Mister Balustealing in Toronto .

What an energy audit entails 

Energy audits are designed to find what’s causing energy loss in your home, but they’re not all created equal. 

Before booking one, confirm what it includes. 

“At the very least, it should consist of a blower-door test (a blower fan is set up in a doorway to measure how much air is leaking in or out of the…
items.t: The Home Audit That Could Save Homeowners Thousands—and Cost You Only $50

items.summary:
A nor'easter and even a " bomb cyclone " are predicted to slam the Northeast on Thanksgiving this year, putting millions in a path of destruction not seen on the holiday for decades. 

Heavy rain, high winds, and coastal impacts to the East Coast are said to begin on Wednesday and carry through Thanksgiving, according to NOAA's Weather Prediction Center .

The biggest impact will be seen starting in the Southeast, before moving its way to the Northeast, Great Lakes, and Ohio Valley.

While flooding is a major consideration, meteorologists are more concerned about the powerful winds accompanying the storm, which could result in tree damage , power outages , and other disasters for homeowners to contend with on the big day. 

The nor’easter 

The storm will ramp up in the Southeast on Wednesday, according to The Weather Channel , with rain, wind, and coastal flooding causing hazardous conditions for travelers heading home for the holiday. 

Because temperatures have dropped as well, snow is also likely in parts of Missouri and Illinois beginning later in the day, continuing into the night, into Thanksgiving.

By Thanksgiving Thursday, the storm will have made its way north into the mid-Atlantic and Ohio Valley, before steadily moving into New England by afternoon or evening. 

While wind is top of mind given the milestone parade, significant coastal flooding along the East Coast is poised to cause beach erosion, flooded coastal streets, and potential structural damage.

Moderate to major flooding is possible from Georgia to Long Island, alongside at least minor flooding in…
items.t: Thanksgiving Nor’easter Could Leave Homeowners In The Dark: Where Power Outages are Likeliest Over The Holiday

items.title: New-Home Sales Surge as Builders Slash Prices to Move Inventory
items.summary:
New -home sales surged in October as prices dropped, according to the latest data from the U.S. Census Bureau.

Sales of new single-family homes hit 701,000 in October, 14.2% above what they were in September and 7.5% above October 2025. Meanwhile, the median sales price hit $391,300, 0.3% below September 2026 and 3.2% below October 2025.

That was driven entirely by a surge in the South, which saw a 36.2% increase from last month and a 24.7% increase from October 2025. Northeast sales plummeted 40.0% month over month and 63.4% year over year, and the Midwest and West also saw declines.

This comes after new-home sales fell 0.6% month over month, 5.3% year over year in September, to 676,000. New-home sales were running 2.9% below 2025 numbers, Realtor.com® economists found. The median sales price in September for new homes fell 3.9% year over year to $400,400.

Realtor.com Senior Economist Joel Berner noted that new home sales are still 3% below where they were in the first 10 months of 2025. And housing inventory remains low.

"Builders are lowering prices to meet demand, and the median new home sales price remains well below the median existing home sales price ," Berner said.

The National Association of Home Builders found that new homes are nearly $40,000 less expensive than existing homes. Single-family housing starts rose 4% last month amid an uneven year . The latest Realtor.com quarterly construction insights report shows that prices on new homes are holding steady, but builders are having to get creative to attract buyers.

Meanwhile, major homebuilders have…
items.t: New-Home Sales Surge as Builders Slash Prices to Move Inventory

items.title: Mortgage Applications Rise to Their Highest Level in 5 Weeks Despite Rise in Rates
items.summary:
Mortgage applications increased last week, despite high interest rates, inflation concerns, and a wobbly stock market. 

For the week ending Nov. 20, the  Mortgage Bankers Association's Market Composite Index —a measure of total mortgage loan application volume—increased 6.1% on a seasonally adjusted basis from one week earlier.

The Purchase Index, which measures the volume of  mortgage applications  to purchase a single-family home, increased 5% from one week earlier after seasonal adjustment, though purchase applications are down 16% from a year ago.

The average contract interest rate for 30-year fixed mortgages with conforming loan balances jumped to 7.38% this week, an increase from last week's rate of 7.31%, according to MBA calculations, and it's the highest level in five weeks.

A separate survey from Freddie Mac showed mortgage rates rose to 7.28%, up from   7.11%  last week. A year ago at this time, the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 6.26%.

"While mortgage rates increased slightly on a weekly average basis, rates declined over the course of the week, which likely spurred purchase application activity,” said Joel Kan , MBA’s vice president and deputy chief economist.

“Purchase applications reached their strongest weekly pace since September but remained well behind last year’s pace," he added. 

Kan also noted that the share of borrowers relying on riskier adjustable-rate mortgage loans jumped to 11.5%—its highest level in more than a year.

"At 6.39%, the ARM mortgage rate was nearly a full percentage lower than the 30-year fixed rate last week," he…
items.t: Mortgage Applications Rise to Their Highest Level in 5 Weeks Despite Rise in Rates

items.title: Oven Fires Surge This Time of Year—Here Is How Homeowners Can Protect Their Kitchen Over the Holidays
items.summary:
Let’s face it: The holiday season is when our ovens are working overtime. 

After all, between long cooking times for the turkey, the myriad side dishes, and multiple batches of cookies we’re making, this is the season when we put this appliance through the paces. 

Unfortunately, it’s also the prime time for an oven fire.

MoneyGeek recently analyzed seven years of fire department reports to the National Fire Incident Reporting System and compared each state's Thanksgiving Day cooking fires with its own average November day, from 2019 to 2025. Nationally, departments reported 3.72 times as many residential cooking fires on Thanksgiving .

And it's not just the turkey that could get ruined. 

While a professional kitchen remodel averages $26,994, depending on the scope of the project and the location, according to Angi.com , fire damage might amp up that pricetag depending on whether cabinets, drywall, appliances, or partial finishes need to be removed and replaced.

Major structural damage can reach $100,000 if flames or water damaged wiring and plumbing or if the fire spread to adjacent rooms.

This is why experts recommend tried and true precautions homeowners can take to keep their home safe.

From 2019 to 2025, fire departments reported 3.72 times as many residential cooking fires on Thanksgiving as on an average nonholiday November day, according to MoneyGeek. (MoneyGeek) 

Take the time to clean 

In the days leading up to the holidays, be sure to inspect the inside of your oven.

items.title: Foreign Buyers Pull Back From U.S., but Canadian Snowbirds Widen Their Lead
items.summary:
Foreign homebuyers retreated from the U.S. housing market this fall, driven by an exodus of European shoppers. This shift helped Canadians cement their dominance. 

Between July and September 2026, global house hunters accounted for 1.3% of traffic on Realtor.com® , down from 1.5% a year ago, according to the latest quarterly International Demand report released on Wednesday.

Realtor.com senior economist Jiayi Xu attributes the broader slowdown to a combination of factors, including geopolitical uncertainty, shifting trade policies, and persistent inflation challenges.

Yet against that downturn, Canada's share of demand has expanded, climbing to 35.9% of overall international traffic and reinforcing its hold on the top spot among foreign buyers.

This development marks a turnaround from a year ago, when Canadian interest in U.S. real estate dipped to 32.3% amid President Donald Trump 's aggressive tariff policies , which defined the beginning of his second term in office.

Sun-soaked Florida remains the premier destination for Canadian snowbirds escaping freezing Northern winters, commanding nearly 29% of Canada's search traffic.

Meanwhile, Texas edged past California as the second-most popular market for Canadians, drawing 8.8% of traffic compared with the Golden State's 8.6%.

"I’m seeing continued interest from Canadian buyers in Southern California," Daniel Zakharia , an agent with Douglas Elliman Beverly Hills , tells Realtor.com. "While political and economic uncertainty prompted some Canadian homeowners to reconsider their U.S. real estate holdings in 2025,…

The 1990s "ended with Columbine and started with the Menendez brothers , the Susan Smith murder, the OJ trial ,” showrunner Richard LaGravenese said in a statement . “I was fascinated by the challenge of doing something that was a murder mystery without an ending, without being solved.”

To portray the effects of the media coverage that surrounded the case, the limited series will focus on Patsy and John Ramsey (played by Melissa McCarthy and Clive Owen ) as well as a group of local and federal investigators (brought to life by Garrett Hedlund , Will Patton , Shea Whigham , and Alison Pill ).

“They all had different points of view for all different reasons,” LaGravenese said. “It was an incredible story to tell from all these perspectives.”

items.title: Amazon Tiny Homes Are Listed for Almost $25,000—but Can You Actually Live in Them?
items.summary:
As home prices and mortgage rates have climbed in recent years, homebuyers and developers alike have turned to factory-built tiny homes as a potential solution for affordable housing.

While low prices and fast shipping make prefab homes from Amazon look like a bargain, buyers should be aware of several factors with this purchase—starting with the fact that selling them is actually prohibited on the platform.

Amazon prohibits the sale of habitable tiny homes and prefabricated dwellings, with its Seller Central policy explicitly banning complete prefab homes, tiny house kits marketed as living spaces, modular and container homes, and other factory-built housing units.

So, why then does a search for "prefab tiny homes" bring up thousands of results?

What Amazon ‘tiny homes’ really are 

Many of the tiny homes on Amazon are simple backyard sheds, compliant with the retailer's rules. Others walk a fine line.

Several listings, which fall between $20,000 and $25,000, use words like “ prefabricated steel building ” and “ expandable modular container. ”

The highlights for one now unlisted item described it as “a portable, multi-purpose outdoor structure for storage, workspace, display, or commercial utility use.” It goes on to say that it has “versatile non-residential use—suitable for office setup, equipment storage, pop-up workspace, site unit, studio, or backyard utility structure.”

Nowhere in the description did it call itself a home or use words like "residential" or "habitation."

Despite Amazon’s ban on the sale of habitable tiny homes, many listings, like this…
items.t: Amazon Explicitly Bans Tiny Homes—Here’s How Sellers Are Sneaking $20K Prefabs Onto the Site Anyway

items.title: If the AI Bubble Pops, Here’s What It Means for Your Home’s Value
items.summary:
When artificial intelligence giant Anthropic went public last week, its $1.494 trillion valuation exceeded the combined value of every owner-occupied home in the San Francisco metropolitan area, according to research from Realtor.com® .

Less than a week later, the company's shares fell below their IPO price , as a renewed sell-off in tech stocks stoked fears that the AI bubble may already be bursting.

“This is how the exuberance ends—not with a whimper but with a bang,” Nobel Prize-winning economist Paul Krugman wrote on Monday .

Krugman, who warned of America's housing bubble as early as 2005, acknowledges he's less certain about AI valuations than he was about home prices two decades ago. But earlier this month, he warned that an AI bust would almost certainly trigger a recession, potentially more painful than the one that followed the dot-com crash.

Others on Wall Street aren't so sure. Many investors remain confident in the industry's fundamentals and see the sell-off as a necessary correction rather than the end of the boom.

But after years of a bull market powered by a handful of AI darlings, new research from Realtor.com finds evidence that the resulting fortunes have helped shape some of America’s most expensive housing markets.

Now, a reversal of those gains could threaten a source of wealth far more central to the financial lives of middle-class Americans: their homes.

How AI wealth has spilled into the housing market 

Anthropic's IPO alone was expected to mint around 2,800 millionaires among its current and former employees, according to estimates from…
items.t: If the AI Bubble Pops, Here’s What It Means for Your Home’s Value

items.title: Iowa Residents Told To Evacuate or Shelter in Place as U.S. Army Prepares To Detonate Nearly 10,000 Pounds of a Lead Explosive
items.summary:
The U.S. Army plans to detonate 9,700 pounds of a lead-based explosive in Southeast Iowa on Wednesday, despite concerns from environmental groups.

The detonation is scheduled to go ahead at 10 a.m. on Wednesday at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, IA. This comes after a lawsuit was filed by the Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club Iowa Chapter asking the federal appeals court to halt the plan.

Two rapid, controlled detonations were initially scheduled to take place last Friday, but the plans were pushed to Wednesday due to a combination of public concern and weather optimization.

Set to be detonated are 68 drums of degraded lead azide, adding up to roughly 9,700 pounds, which have become sensitive and unstable. It is the primary explosive used to initiate munitions

A controlled detonation is now the only viable option, according to the Army’s Q&A page about the event.

As lead azide degrades, it crystalizes and becomes sensitive to temperature changes, shock, and friction, making it unsafe to move. There are chemical neutralization procedures, but the drums are too unstable for the physical manipulation this option requires, according to the Army.

The U.S. Army will detonated about 9,700 pounds of lead azide in Middletown, IA, on Wednesday. (Photo by Scott Olson/Getty Images) 

Inside the plan to detonate a lead-based explosive 

U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Region 7 Director Jim Macy wrote a letter to Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds , ensuring her that the EPA was working alongside the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and the…
items.t: Iowa Residents Told To Evacuate or Shelter in Place as U.S. Army Prepares To Detonate Nearly 10,000 Pounds of a Lead Explosive

items.summary:
The Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything” takes place in the Theranos founder’s former Del Mar, CA , rental—and the property’s location in an exclusive, gated community could be just part of the reason the film’s unexpected release was such a smash.

The project—which is now available to stream on demand and was directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim —was kept secret for the four years it was in production, leaving viewers in awe after the documentary’s surprise Sept. 6 premiere at Telluride Film Festival.

Holmes and her partner, Billy Evans , invited the film crew—which Oppenheim told Variety was intentionally kept intimate to keep the project a secret—to reside in the guesthouse of the home for the 34 days before she reported to Federal Prison Camp in Bryan, TX , on May 30, 2023.

“Keeping it under wraps was very important because we never wanted to get in front of what we were capturing,” the director shared.

The crew would typically shoot for 16-hour days, with Fielder telling Variety that cameras were strategically positioned to “cover the whole house” so nothing would be missed.

Directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim worked tirelessly to keep the film's creation "under wraps." (JC Olivera/Getty Images) 

The documentary takes place in Elizabeth Holmes' ultraprivate rental in an exclusive and gated community in Del Mar, CA. (Google Earth) 

The community has only about a dozen residences and is guarded around the clock. (Google Earth) 

The four-bedroom, four-bathroom beachfront property is located in an ultraprivate community less…
items.t: Inside Elizabeth Holmes’ Secret Oceanfront Rental Seen in ‘You Can See Everything’ Documentary a Month Before She’s Sent to Prison

items.title: Jessica Alba Ordered To Pay Cash Warren $577K—Inside Her Recent Beverly Hills Real Estate Moves
items.summary:
Jessica Alba ’s divorce from Cash Warren is back in the headlines after a new court order awarded Warren $577,481 from Alba’s retirement benefits. 

The ruling comes after the former couple sold their longtime Beverly Hills –area home and Alba later purchased another property in the area.

The retirement award comes from Alba’s account in the HonorBar Inc. Profit Sharing Plan, according to court documents reported by TMZ . 

Any money left in the account after Warren receives his share is to go to Alba. The documents also allow Warren to take the award as a lump sum or move it into an individual retirement account or another retirement plan.

The court order also addresses account records: If Warren requests statements in writing within the next year, Alba must provide them within 10 days.

Jessica Alba’s divorce from Cash Warren is back in the headlines after a new court order awarded Warren $577,481 from Alba’s retirement benefits. (Taylor Hill/Getty Images) 

According to the outlet, transferring the money into a retirement account could avoid a 20% tax withholding. 

The ruling is the latest financial development following the couple’s divorce, which was finalized in February 2026.

It was previously reported that Alba was ordered to pay Warren $3 million to balance the division of their assets. 

Their settlement also divided interests in several companies, shares in The Honest Company, and residuals from projects made during their marriage. 

Meanwhile, Alba and Warren have already put their real estate ties behind them.

Their former Beverly Hills–area home was sold…
items.t: Jessica Alba Ordered To Pay Cash Warren $577K—Inside Her Recent Beverly Hills Real Estate Moves

items.title: Derek Hough Recalls Difficult Utah Upbringing with Neighbors Who ‘Terrorized’ Family Before Moving to London
items.summary:
Derek Hough is opening up about his upbringing, sharing painful details from his childhood in his new Hulu documentary, “The Symphony of Dance.”

In the film, the “Dancing with the Stars" judge returns to his childhood home in Utah , and details the challenging environment he was raised in.

“The neighborhood that we grew up in, we definitely just had some neighbors that weren’t great,” Derek, 41, explained. “They pretty much terrorized my family in a lot of ways.”

“They hung me up in a tree by my ankles. They put a gun to my head, spat on me, hogtied me up in a field and left me there,” he continued. “One of my neighbors was, for lack of a better word, really inappropriate with me, physically.”

Eventually, Derek’s parents separated, and the family moved across town to an apartment building where his mother and father lived in units across the hall from one another.

Derek Hough is opening up about his challenging childhood in the new Hulu documentary, "The Symphony of Dance." (Disney via Getty Images) 

The biographical film unpacks Derek's past, as well as wife Hayley Erbert Hough's life-changing brain injury. (Disney via Getty Images) 

“I remember moving away from there and feeling relieved,” he said. However, the move didn’t solve all of his problems, and he continued to struggle in the wake of his parents’ divorce.

“I just didn’t understand where I was going. I didn’t understand what I was doing,” he said. “I was just kind of left to my own devices as a 12-year-old. I would skip school. I would skip dance, just floating around with no direction.”

Although he had…
items.t: Derek Hough Recalls Difficult Utah Upbringing with Neighbors Who ‘Terrorized’ Family Before Moving to London

items.title: Can a Solar Generator Actually Keep Your Lights On During an Outage—or Is It Just Expensive Hype?
items.summary:
Winter storm season is fast approaching, with even Thanksgiving being primed for power outages across the country. 

If you’d like to limit its disruption on your everyday life, generators may be top of mind.

As you do your research, you may come across solar generators and wonder how they compare to other options.

“A solar generator uses sunlight as its fuel. It also happens to be clean, quiet, and quick,” explains Ben Zook , founder and owner of Belmont Solar , a solar installation company in Gordonville, PA . 

While a solar generator will likely be more expensive upfront, it could be a smart investment, depending on your location and goals. 

By understanding how it works as well as its limitations, you can decide whether it’s the right backup solution for your home .

What is a solar generator? 

The name “solar generator” is a bit misleading. 

This device is actually a portable battery system you can refill with solar panels and use when you don’t have power. 

It includes a built-in inverter that converts DC electricity into AC electricity, which most household appliances use. In addition, it might come with USB ports to charge electronic devices such as cellphones. 

So, how does the recharging process work?

“Put simply, solar panels convert sunlight into electricity. When sunlight hits the panels, it produces an electric current,” explains Fox Swim , senior industry researcher at Aurora Solar in Nanaimo, British Columbia .

Keep in mind that a solar generator doesn’t provide unlimited power. It’s limited by your battery’s capacity and how much electricity your…
items.t: Can a Solar Generator Actually Keep Your Lights On During an Outage—or Is It Just Expensive Hype?

items.title: Miley Cyrus’ Wedding Venue Was Frank Sinatra’s Former Palm Springs Home—and It’s Available as a Vacation Rental
items.summary:
After a stunning ceremony in Palm Springs, CA , Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando are officially husband and wife—and part of the history of an iconic midcentury modern estate that formerly belonged to Frank Sinatra .

The musicians said “I do” on Nov. 21, surrounded by family, friends, and a bounty of stunning flowers. The picturesque celebration took place in the backyard of Twin Palms, right on the edge of the piano-shaped pool the “Fly Me to the Moon” singer once lounged by, according to Elle Decor .

Commissioned by Sinatra in 1947, the 4,500-square-foot home is located in the Movie Colony , a legendary Palm Springs neighborhood that Hollywood entertainers flocked to in the 1930s and 1940s.

The official Twin Palms website explains that Sinatra came to the desert town in hopes of finding a weekend retreat for his family after signing a movie contract with MGM Studios. He was initially looking for a Georgian-style estate with a lavish brick facade, but architect E. Stewart Williams persuaded him to go for something more “desert appropriate.”

Miley Cyrus married musician Maxx Morando in a beautiful ceremony at Frank Sinatra's former Palm Springs, CA, estate. (Taylor Hill/FilmMagic) 

The home was commissioned by the "Fly Me to the Moon" singer in 1947. (Getty Images ) 

Although Sinatra originally wanted a Georgian estate, architect E. Stewart Williams persuaded him to go for something more "dessert appropriate." (Getty Images ) 

Today, the renovated dwelling is available as a vacation rental, private event venue, or commercial use space. (Getty Images)

items.title: Condo vs. Townhouse: Which Investment Will Turn Around More Equity After a Decade?
items.summary:
Between 2014 and 2024, the difference in price appreciation between condos and single-family homes was less than 5 percentage points nationally, according to an analysis from Realtor.com® . Townhouses came even closer to matching the performance of detached homes—trailing by just 0.8 percentage points.

It's a remarkable outcome for the buyers opted out of the which picket fence dream, and instead invested in properties that often offer a more affordable entry point into homeownership. But that outcome may be harder to replicate in today's rapidly changing housing market.

Condo values fell 0.8% year over year in August 2026, even as single-family home values rose 1.8%, according to data from Intercontinental Exchange . And as home price growth cools, expenses that were easier to stomach during years of rapid appreciation stand to take a bigger bite out of homeowners' returns.

Even so, those national numbers tell only part of the story. In some regions, condos substantially outperformed townhouses over the decade examined by Realtor.com, challenging the notion that owning a piece of land necessarily leads to stronger appreciation.

Understanding what drove those differences—and how the economics of owning each property type are changing—offers some clues as to where buyers might find the greatest opportunity to build equity over the next decade.

Neck-and-neck appreciation nationally 

Single-family homes appreciated 87.3% from 2014 to 2024, according to Realtor.com senior economist Hannah Jones . Townhomes nearly matched that pace at 86.5%, while condos trailed only…
items.t: Condo vs. Townhouse: Which Investment Will Turn Around More Equity After a Decade?

items.title: AnnaLynne McCord Looks Back on the ‘Days of Our Lives’ Role That ‘Saved’ Her—Months After Her Backyard Wedding at Her L.A. Home
items.summary:
AnnaLynne McCord was still processing a call about her finances when her phone rang again. This time, it was the casting director of “Days of Our Lives” with a job offer.

In an interview with Hollywood Hills Magazine , the actress, 39, said joining the soap “saved” her. McCord had spent five seasons starring on “90210” after appearing on “Ugly Betty” and “Greek.” 

By 2024, when the “Days” offer came along, she was worried about how she would cover her bills.

“I was told that I could not pay my credit cards. You work in this industry, and it’s sobering because you can be at the highest highs, and then things shift,” McCord told the magazine.

McCord said she had devoted much of her time to charity work. That morning, she found herself asking a question about her own future: “Am I going to be okay?”

AnnaLynne McCord was still processing a call about her finances when her phone rang again. This time, it was the casting director of “Days of Our Lives” with a job offer. (JOCE/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images) 

“That afternoon, Marnie, the casting director of Days of our Lives , called me asking if I want to come on the show, and I said, ‘Yes, I do’, in more ways than she would ever know,” McCord recalled.

Looking back, McCord described that call as a “foundational moment of what Days would go on to offer me.” The job came along when she needed the work. 

What surprised her over time was how much the people she worked with would come to mean to her.

“I feel at home here. I feel family here. I feel that people genuinely care about your well-being,” she told Hollywood Hills…
items.t: AnnaLynne McCord Looks Back on the ‘Days of Our Lives’ Role That ‘Saved’ Her—Months After Her Backyard Wedding at Her L.A. Home

items.title: National Home Value Growth Holds Steady, Yet Miami Outperforms
items.summary:
National growth in home values was flat month over month in September as mortgage rates accelerated and inflation continued running hot. 

The value of single-family homes as measured by repeat transactions increased 2.1% year over year, same as in August, according to data from the  S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Index  released on Tuesday.

However, home values fell in real terms for the 16th consecutive month, as September's 3.7% inflation rate outpaced the home value gain by roughly 1.6 percentage points, up from about 1.3 points in August.

"Nominal home prices remain resilient, but inflation is once again widening the gap between nominal and real housing returns," says Rebecca Kaufman , associate director of commodities at S&P Dow Jones Indices.

Across the 20 cities tracked by the index,  Chicago  yet again led the U.S. with a 6.9% annual gain. New York City  took second place with a year-over-year increase of 5.8%, but Miami emerged as the month's surprise, finishing third with a 4.6% gain.

"Miami’s rise is particularly notable," points out Kaufman. "After moving into fourth place among the 20 cities in July and August, it has now climbed into the top three, a sharp reversal from its comparatively weak performance in 2025."

(Realtor.com) 

On the other side of the spectrum, Seattle recorded the largest annual decline for the fourth consecutive
month at 1.9%, followed by Denver (-1.0%) and Dallas (-0.9%), reflecting a persistent regional divergence. 

September also revealed a widening gap between seasonal weakness and underlying price momentum. On a nonseasonally…
items.t: National Home Value Growth Holds Steady Yet Miami Outperforms

items.title: Council tax and stamp duty: both are a disaster zone. Scrap them and start from scratch | Polly Toynbee
items.summary:
These ancient and often grossly unfair taxes are stifling the economy and young people. It’s long past time for radical reform

When voters were asked in 2020 which tax they would cut first, council tax came out on top, and rightly so. Still, it’s taken six years for an array of Labour and Liberal Democrat MPs to call for reforms to this most grotesquely unjust tax.

Prompted by a public petition organised by the campaign Fairer Share, a Westminster Hall debate heard calls for a review into property taxes, which would lay out options for replacing council tax and stamp duty land tax. Labour MPs were among those who have signed a letter to Downing Street calling for property tax reform to be a priority in Andy Burnham’s upcoming 10-year plan. Among flotillas of economists and thinktanks who signed the letter is Lord O’Neill, a Burnham adviser and former Goldman Sachs economist, who calls UK property taxation “utterly nonsensical”. Burnham has frequently backed reform of the “highly regressive” council tax and stamp duty, labelling them as “a tax on the aspiration of young people”.

Polly Toynbee is a Guardian columnist

Continue reading...
items.t: Council tax and stamp duty: both are a disaster zone. Scrap them and start from scratch | Polly Toynbee

items.title: Cost of renting in Britain to rise twice as fast as buying amid shortage of properties
items.summary:
Rents to rise by 14% until at least 2029, Hamptons predicts, as high demand for properties and low supply push up costs for tenants

The cost of renting a home in Britain is expected to rise about twice as fast as that of buying one until at least 2029, according to research, with shrinking supply pushing up the prices paid by tenants.

Rents on newly agreed lets are forecast to grow by 14.2% between 2026 and 2029, compared with house price growth of 7.2%, according to forecasts from estate agent Hamptons.

Continue reading...
items.t: Cost of renting in Britain to rise twice as fast as buying amid shortage of properties
